content:
Finally, after 3 months of very intensive, nonstop work by several AI agents (Codex and Claude Code), we have settled a classification of all 15,973 semigroups of order 6. Every one of the 15,969 that has a finite basis now has it written down explicitly, and the remaining 4 are proved to have none at all. The whole list of bases is produced for the first time in history. Until now, for most of these semigroups, mathematicians only knew that a basis exists; nobody had ever written one down. The formalization in Lean, orchestrated with a multi-agent approach, reached more than 5 million lines of verified Lean code, one of the largest auto-formalization projects to date. It's been an amazing joint work with Mikolas Janota and Jan Hula, accompanied by senior experts in semigroup theory, João Araújo and Edmond W. H. Lee.

MATH-AI NeurIPS 2026 paper: https://people.ciirc.cvut.cz/~janotmik/mathai26.pdf
GitHub repo: https://github.com/nasqret/semibase-order6
Semibase explorer: nasqret.github.io/semibase-site
X annoucement: https://x.com/nasqret/status/2106136282061574579

Congrats! Now do the 836,021 semigroups of order 7. Or order 8... :smile:

Any idea how much this could be golfed?

Justin Asher said:

Congrats! Now do the 836,021 semigroups of order 7. Or order 8... :smile:

Any idea how much this could be golfed?

Thanks! We actually did a lot of work in degree 7. Most of the techniques discovered for degree 6 can be reused in degree 7 and there are some new challenges. The major one is that we don't know yet a complete list of finitely based semigroups! Order 8 is still a bit far but I managed to prove concrete results about specific semigroups of order 9. I think the code can still be very much simplified.

Bartosz Naskręcki said:

Most of the techniques discovered for degree 6 can be reused in degree 7 and there are some new challenges.

Huh, this is interesting. I wonder if you could extend your semibase-site to a larger "semigroup database" like the LMFDB that collects results about all degrees, hopefully working towards a future classification theorem.

Jack McCarthy said:

Huh, this is interesting. I wonder if you could extend your semibase-site to a larger "semigroup database" like the LMFDB that collects results about all degrees, hopefully working towards a future classification theorem.

Yes, this is exactly our plan for the coming months. We talked with Araujo and he is interested to turn every single piece of knowledge in the literature about finite semigroups into a reusable artifact. I have not decided what could be the universal format for each such page but we have data which can be regenerated to any form that is requested. I am particularly interested in developing a functional code base where every researcher in this area can use and build on top of that. In this project we have already discovered some corrections to the existing literature.
